milestone: PR9 default command-WAL public raw KV cutover
features: public Set/Delete/Batch.Write raw KV writes routed to RawKVBatch typed command frames
public command-WAL mode proof through treedb.write_path.mode=command_wal_cached
cached public command-WAL writes with the legacy cached redo journal disabled
physical backend flush batches that do not emit duplicate RawKVBatch command frames
checkpoint/close publication of covered command-WAL LSNs after cached flush
reopen from persisted command_wal_v1 without explicit backend-only APIs
public raw KV microbenchmark coverage for point Set and batched RawKVBatch writes

performance_gate.rationale: Public command-WAL writes now use the cached write path instead of direct backend root publication per point Set. The short smoke no longer shows the prior direct-backend cliff: point Set improved from the earlier 953.5 sets/s to 163034 sets/s, and the longer 5000x point run measured 620162 sets/s. Batched writes are within parity in the 64-op case and faster than cached legacy in the 1024-op case. Point Set remains slower than cached legacy due typed command-frame encode/append overhead, but it is same-order cached throughput rather than tracker-blocking direct-backend throughput.

unsupported_modes: Update/UpdateSync remain rejected under cached public command-WAL until they have typed command coverage
DeleteRange remains rejected under cached public command-WAL until it has typed command coverage
next_required_work: continue optimizing point Set command-frame encode/append overhead if a stricter parity floor is adopted
rerun unified_bench treedb vs treedb_command_wal batch_write and point-write modes after CI review settles
